rationale: This benchmark is dominated by tight, hot numeric loops (test_variable*, loop_invariant, constant_folding kernels) under a timing harness, so runtime cost is the binding constraint: SUB is weighted aggressively (cheap arithmetic substitution, high diversity on simple integer/char types, near-zero risk), and SPLIT stays enabled at modest weight since it is low-cost structural diversity that composes well with FLA; FLA is kept as the primary control-flow defense (highest SecurityGain) but its RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights are set high enough to steer it toward the large cold functions (main at 6.7KB) rather than the inner-loop kernels; BCF is retained at low priority with high RuntimeCost/SizeCost and a moderate CorrectnessRisk because its opaque-predicate overhead is painful in invariant loops and it adds little beyond FLA+SUB; IBR is a middle-weight complement for branch hiding with acceptable loop overhead; ICALL is included but low-weighted since this code has few indirect-call sites (mostly template/static dispatch) and virtualizing calls risks breaking the benchmark's timing semantics; IGV is the weakest fit because the program is computation-bound with few mutable globals worth encrypting, so it is weighted toward being selected only where features genuinely favor it.
